text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock dropped 7.4% today, extending a two-week decline of 8.6%. The immediate trigger was a sharp reversal in oil prices: yesterday crude fell on news of diplomatic talks between Iran and Saudi Arabia aimed at de-escalating regional tensions, and today it fell further after Iran's supreme leader signaled conditions for ending the conflict. When geopolitical risk that had pushed oil higher suddenly eases, refiners face headwinds — lower crude prices can squeeze their margins, especially if they've locked in higher input costs or if refined product prices don't fall as fast.

The broader context here is a whipsaw in energy markets tied to Middle East tensions. Just days ago, on October 23rd, Brent crude hit a six-month high above $116 on concerns about supply disruptions from Iranian-backed attacks and regional conflict. That rally benefited refiners by lifting the value of their output. The shift toward diplomacy and de-escalation has reversed that risk premium almost as quickly, and oil falling from $115+ globally back toward $108 domestically removes the geopolitical "floor" that had been supporting refiner margins.
